verses.1: Having crossed the vast, beautiful kingdom of Kosala, the sagacious elder brother of Lakshmana stood facing Ayodhya with folded palms and said:
verses.2: O Ayodhya, the best of cities ruled by those born in the Kakutstha race I take leave of you and of all those gods inhabiting and guarding you.
verses.3: On completion of exile and my filial obligations to king Dasaratha, lord of the world, discharged, I shall, reunited with my parents, see you again.
verses.4: He looked miserable, his copperred eyes filled with tears. He raised his right hand and said to the villagers who had come to see him:
verses.5: You have aptly shown your kindness and compassion to me. It is not proper to prolong one's grief. So do go and altend to your duties.
verses.6: All of them paid their homage by circumambulating the highsouled Rama. Crying bitterly, they stood here and there.
verses.7: Not yet satisfied (they wanted to linger longer), they stood weeping, while Rama went out of sight just as the Sun disappears at nightfall.
verses.8: Rama, the best of men, crossed the auspicious land of Kosala which was worth seeing by kings. It looked charming with sacrificial posts and altars, pleasure gardens and mango groves and tanks filled with water. It was rich with herds of cattle, wealth and foodgrains. It was inhabited by charitable, contented and wellnourished people free from fear from any quarter. And it reverberated with the sounds of Vedic recitations.

It looked charming with sacrificial posts and altars, pleasure gardens and mango groves and tanks filled with water. It was rich with herds of cattle, wealth and foodgrains. verses.11: Rama, the greatest among those endowed with fortitude, travelled through the middle of the kingdom which was pleasing, prosperous and full of ravishing gardens fit to be enjoyed by kings.
verses.12: There Rama saw the holy Ganga flowing in three (worlds) with her sacred waters, free from moss, and worshipped by sages.
verses.13: The holy Ganga, adorned with graceful hermitages situated not far away is visited at times by delightful nymphs who sport in her lakes.
verses.14: The Ganga is graced by devatas, danavas, gandharvas and kinneras. Wives of several gandharvas always visit this auspicious river.
verses.15: Since this river flows through heavens for the gods, it is wellknown as 'Devapadmini' where celestial lotuses grow. The river embraces hundreds of hills serving as sporting places and pleasuregardens for gods.
verses.16: The sound of dashing waters of the Ganga is like her laughter and the foam like her sparkling smile. Here she flows straight like the braid of a maiden and there in whirlpools.
verses.17: Here the Ganga runs deep but quiet, there she looks perturbed due to fastflowing waters, here she flows with a deep groan and there with a dreadful roar.
verses.18: Here hosts of celestials take their ablutions and there she shines with lilies of pure blue. Here her banks are curved and there her bed is dotted with patches of white sand.
verses.19: The river reverberates with the cries of swans, cranes and chakravakas (ruddy goose). It rings intermittently with the chirpings of birds charged with endless pasison.
verses.20: Here on her banks stand trees adorned as though with garlands, and there in her waters abound fullblown lilies and a forest of lotuses.
verses.21: Here she is decked with hosts of waterlilies and halfblown flowers while elsewhere she looks intoxicated with the pollen fallen from various flowers.
verses.22: The river, cleansed of heaps of impurities, appears like a transparent gem. The interiors of forests on her banks always resounds with the trumpeting of mighty, intoxicated, wild elephants guarding the quarters, fit to be the vehicles of gods.
verses.23: Just like a lady, Ganga is decorated with the best of ornaments her banks are filled with fruits, flowers, tender leaves or shoots and (flowering) shrubs. It is inhabited by birds and brahmins and infested with sisumaras (small whales), crocodiles and serpents.
verses.24: Just like a lady, Ganga is decorated with the best of ornaments her banks are filled with fruits, flowers, tender leaves or shoots and (flowering) shrubs. It is inhabited by birds and brahmins and infested with sisumaras (small whales), crocodiles and serpents.
verses.25: Mightyarmed Rama reached Srngaberapura on the bank of this consort of the ocean, this Ganga loud with the cries of kraunchas and herons. This sinless, divine Ganga, destroyer of sins who flows from the feet of lord Visnu and by the effulgence (penance) of Sagara's son (Bhagiratha) emerged from the matted locks of lord Siva.
verses.26: Mightyarmed Rama reached Srngaberapura on the bank of this consort of the ocean, this Ganga loud with the cries of kraunchas and herons. This sinless, divine Ganga, destroyer of sins who flows from the feet of lord Visnu and by the effulgence (penance) of Sagara's son (Bhagiratha) emerged from the matted locks of lord Siva.
verses.27: Beholding river Ganga full of waves and whirlpools, the great chariotwarrior (Rama) said to Sumantra: We shall spend the night here.
verses.28: "Not far from the river, charioteer, is this very great ingudi tree rich in flowers and shoots. Let us lodge here."
verses.29: "Let me behold the best of rivers, auspicious, whose waters are honoured by gods and men and gandharvas, by beasts and serpents and birds."
verses.30: Lakshmana and Sumantra said to Raghava, "So be it," and then drove up with the horses to that ingudi tree.
verses.31: Rama, the delight of the Ikshvakus, came to that lovely tree and descended from the chariot with his wife and with Lakshmana.
verses.32: Sumantra too descended, unyoked the excellent horses, and waited with joined palms upon Rama, who was seated at the foot of the tree.
verses.33: There was a king there named Guha, a friend to Rama as his own self, mighty, of the Nishada race, and renowned as a chief.
verses.34: Hearing that Rama, the tiger among men, had come to his realm, he came attended by the elders, by his ministers and by his kinsmen.
verses.35: Then, seeing the lord of the Nishadas approaching from afar, Rama went with Saumitri to meet Guha.
verses.36: Stricken, Guha embraced him and said to Raghava: "As Ayodhya is, so is this yours, Rama. What shall I do for you?"
verses.37: "Who indeed shall obtain so beloved a guest, mighty-armed one?" Then, taking up excellent food and provision of many kinds,
verses.38: he swiftly presented the guest-offering and spoke these words: "Welcome to you, mighty-armed one. This whole earth is yours."
verses.39: "We are your servants and your honour is our lord; rule our kingdom well. Food to chew and to eat, to drink and to lick, is ready, and choice couches for you, and fodder for the horses."
verses.40: As he spoke thus, Raghava replied to Guha: "By you we have at all times been honoured and gladdened,
verses.41: "by your coming on foot and by this show of affection." And pressing him with his two well-rounded arms, he spoke these words:
verses.42: "By good fortune, Guha, I see you in health along with your kinsmen. Is all well too in your realm, among your friends and in your woods?"
verses.43: "Whatever little you have made ready out of affection, I acknowledge it all; but I do not engage in the accepting of gifts."
verses.44: "Know me for an ascetic ranging the forest, wearing kusha and bark and deerskin, living on fruit and root, and set upon dharma."
verses.45: "I have need of fodder for the horses and of nothing else at all; by this much alone shall I be well honoured by you."
verses.46: "These horses were dear to my father, king Dasaratha; if they are well tended, I shall be honoured by them."
verses.47: Guha there and then commanded his men that drink and fodder for the horses be given swiftly.
verses.48: Then, with bark for his upper garment, he performed the evening twilight rite and took water alone for his food, fetched by Lakshmana himself.
verses.49: Then Lakshmana washed the feet of Rama and his wife as they lay upon the ground, and withdrawing, stood leaning against a tree.
verses.50: Guha too, conversing with the charioteer and with Saumitri, kept vigilant watch over Rama, bow in hand.
verses.51: So, as that illustrious, high-minded and great-souled son of Dasaratha lay there, he who had never known sorrow and was accustomed to ease, the night passed very slowly.
